communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Memorandum of Agreement
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

from U.S. Central Command (USCENTCOM), specifically the Command Staff Judge Advocate's office (CCJA) and any other USCENTCOM office(s) that negotiated, hold, or maintain custody of the agreement described below:
 
1. The final, executed copy of the Memorandum of Agreement between the Department of Defense of the United States of America, as represented by U.S. Central Command, and the Ministry of Defense of Israel, regarding the assignment of liaison officers to U.S. Central Command (referred to internally as the "NR-FLO MOA" or "Liaison Officer MOA"), including any signatures, annexes, and effective/entry-into-force dates.
 
2. The April 27, 2021 memorandum from the Defense Technology Security Administration (DTSA), Strategy and Policy Division, International Engagement, approving USCENTCOM's request to negotiate and conclude that MOA (addressed to the USCENTCOM Chief of Staff, attention CDR Sean Purdy), and any subsequent DTSA or Office of the Secretary of Defense/Office of General Counsel correspondence approving, reviewing, or amending the final negotiated text.
 
3. Any records reflecting whether the above MOA has since been amended, extended, renewed, or terminated, including the current status of the agreement as of the date this request is processed.
 
4. Any prior draft versions negotiated between USCENTCOM and the Israeli Ministry of Defense between January 2020 and April 2021 that were superseded by the final version, to the extent USCENTCOM's files distinguish them from the executed agreement in item 1 (I am not requesting an open-ended search of all drafts; only those already identifiable as part of the negotiation history of this specific MOA).
 
This request follows FOIA case 26-F-2857, filed with the OSD/JS FOIA Requester Service Center on July 28, 2026, which sought "all active memoranda of agreement" between the Department of War and Israel's Ministry of Defense. That office administratively closed the request on September 17, 2026, on the grounds that it was not "reasonably described" and that OSD/JS does not process records held by other DoD/DoW components such as combatant commands. This request is narrowed accordingly to a single, specifically identified agreement and its accompanying approval correspondence, held by USCENTCOM rather than OSD/JS.
 
If USCENTCOM is not the correct custodian for any portion of this request, please refer that portion to the appropriate component consistent with 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(C) and notify me of the referral.
  
I am an assistant editor for Reason Magazine, where I cover foreign policy and national security. My reporting is published to a broad public audience at no cost to readers, and I have no commercial interest in these records. Therefore, I request to be categorized as a "representative of the news media" under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(ii)(II) for fee purposes.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: U.S.-Israel innovation agreement
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

from the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) and/or Army Futures Command (please route to whichever component holds the records, and refer any portion held elsewhere consistent with 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(C)):
 
1. Any concluded memorandum of understanding, memorandum of agreement, "arrangement of interest" (AOI), or similar instrument between DEVCOM/Army Futures Command and the Israel Defense Forces' Combat Methods and Innovation Division (Force Build-up Directorate/J8, referred to internally as "Shiluach"), regarding cooperation on innovation and combat-methods development, including but not limited to areas such as artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, sensor technology, and digital transformation of the battlefield.
 
2. Correspondence, briefing materials, or internal memoranda discussing or responding to a proposal for such cooperation that was raised in connection with a visit to the United States by the commanding general of the IDF's "Shiluach" division around August 15-19, 2021, including any DEVCOM or Army Futures Command records reflecting whether that proposal was accepted, formalized, or declined.
 
3. If no such instrument was ultimately concluded, records sufficient to show the disposition of the proposal (e.g., a decision memo, an internal response, or correspondence declining further cooperation).
 
Please interpret this request to cover records dated from January 1, 2021 through the date this request is processed.
  
I am an assistant editor journalist for Reason, where I cover foreign policy and national security. My reporting is published to a broad public audience at no cost to readers, and I have no commercial interest in these records. Therefore, I request to be categorized as a "representative of the news media" under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(ii)(II) for fee purposes.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti
